Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission cycle across every in-scope company code, state and line of business.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Companies Act (Canada) s.367 (report of actuary), s.203 (audit committee), ss.359-364 (revocation, resignation, statements), re-read at filing time; the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call Definitions & Instructions are re-read each reporting cycle (rep: Canada).

In-scope processes.value: MCAS scope confirmation, data extraction/reconciliation, workbook population, independent review, submission, post-filing reconciliation to the statutory Annual Statement, and exam-readiness handoff, across every NAIC company code and state where the group writes Private Passenger Auto, Homeowners, Life, Annuity or LTC business.

In-scope systems.value: NAIC MCAS Data Call system for template download, edit checks and submission; source data pulled from the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse and reconciled to the GL.

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Filing Procedure — scope confirmation, data mapping to interrogatories, workbook build/validation, independent review, submission, and post-filing reconciliation.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually against the current-year MCAS Definitions & Instructions.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per line of business — May 1 for Private Passenger Auto/Homeowners/Life/Annuity, June 1 for LTC and Lender-Placed, per the current NAIC data call notice; tracked per company code and state in the filing calendar.

Deadline reminders configured.value: T-30 (data extract), T-15 (workbook validated), T-7 (reviewed), T-2 (submitted) reminders per line of business, escalating to the Head of Compliance if T-2 is missed.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Workbook, submission confirmation, certification and reconciliation note retained 5 years minimum (extended for any open market conduct exam) in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late submission or material post-filing correction is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every exception's root cause and remediation plan before closure.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every NAIC company code, state and line of business required to file under the current MCAS data call for the reporting year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed deadlines; any submitted figure differing from independently re-pulled source data by more than 1% without a documented explanation is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per line/state; test runs once per cycle over the full population immediately after the data call closes.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any sampled workbook.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS test workpaper (population reconciliation, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: MCAS confirmation numbers, workbooks and reconciliation notes, presentable as a market conduct exam response within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns exam/inquiry responses on MCAS data; Regulatory Reporting Manager supplies source reconciliations.

checklist.step: Confirm MCAS filing scope for the reporting year
actions: In the NAIC MCAS Data Call system (mcas.naic.org), open the current data call and read the participating-state list and line-of-business matrix.
Cross-reference against the company's NAIC company codes and state licenses to confirm every state where the company writes the line is in scope.
Flag any state added or dropped from the data call versus the prior year and notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Record the confirmed scope (companies, states, lines) on the MCAS filing tracker.
checklist.done: the MCAS filing tracker lists every in-scope NAIC company code, state and line of business for the reporting year.

checklist.step: Pull the raw transactional data feeding each MCAS interrogatory
actions: Extract policy counts, premium, claims counts/amounts, complaints, cancellations/non-renewals and underwriting actions by state and line for the full calendar reporting year.
Map each extracted field to its MCAS interrogatory number using the current year's MCAS Definitions & Instructions for that line of business.
Reconcile extracted premium and claims totals to the general ledger and the statutory Annual Statement state page for the same state/line.
Log any reconciling difference over 1% with an explanation and route unresolved items to the Controller.
checklist.done: every MCAS interrogatory has a sourced, GL-reconciled data feed with differences under 1% or explained.

checklist.step: Populate the MCAS submission workbook per line of business
actions: Download the current-year MCAS Excel template for each in-scope line from the NAIC MCAS system.
Enter the reconciled figures into each interrogatory cell, preserving the template's state and column order.
Run the template's built-in validation formulas and resolve every flagged cell before proceeding.
Save one workbook per line named <company>-<line>-MCAS-<year>.xlsx in the filing folder.
checklist.done: a validated MCAS workbook exists for every in-scope line with zero unresolved template flags.

checklist.step: Independently review the populated workbook against source data
actions: Re-trace 100% of the state-level totals in each workbook back to the extract in step 2.
Check the state and line totals sum correctly and no state was silently dropped from the scope list.
Confirm year-over-year swings greater than 25% in any interrogatory carry a written explanation.
Sign and date the review log entry before authorizing upload.
checklist.done: the reviewer has signed off that every workbook total ties to source and every large variance is explained.

checklist.step: Upload and submit the data through the NAIC MCAS Data Call system
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS Data Call system with the company's NAIC user credentials.
Select the reporting year, company code and line of business, then upload the validated workbook.
Run the system's online edit checks and correct any submission-level errors before finalizing.
Click Submit for each company/line combination and capture the confirmation number and timestamp.
checklist.done: every in-scope company/line combination shows a Submitted status with a captured confirmation number.

checklist.step: File the submission confirmation and retain the certification
actions: Download the MCAS system's submission confirmation PDF for each company/line and save it to the filing folder.
Complete the internal MCAS filing certification naming the preparer, reviewer and submission date.
Attach the certification and confirmation PDFs to the MCAS filing tracker row.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager that the filing is complete.
checklist.done: a confirmation PDF and signed certification exist for every submitted company/line, linked in the tracker.

checklist.step: Track the MCAS due date against the NAIC data call calendar
actions: Read the current data call's published due date (May 1 for most lines, June 1 for LTC/Lender-Placed) from the MCAS system's data call notice.
Enter the due date, per line of business, into the compliance filing calendar.
Back-schedule milestones: extract complete T-30, workbook validated T-15, reviewed T-7, submitted T-2.
Confirm the calendar entry owner is the analyst assigned to that line.
checklist.done: the filing calendar carries the correct MCAS due date per line with four dated internal milestones.

checklist.step: Configure deadline reminder alerts
actions: Set automated reminders at T-30, T-15, T-7 and T-2 against each line's MCAS due date.
Add an escalation reminder to the Head of Compliance if T-2 is not marked complete.
Test that the reminder alerts fire correctly.
checklist.done: reminders exist at all four milestones and an escalation trigger fires if T-2 is missed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submitted totals to the statutory Annual Statement once filed
actions: Compare the state page premium/loss totals to the MCAS submission for the same period.
Confirm any difference stems only from timing or scope differences allowed by the MCAS instructions.
File the reconciliation note with the MCAS filing tracker row for the year.
checklist.done: the post-filing reconciliation note is complete and attached, with any variance explained.

checklist.step: Respond to NAIC MCAS system edit-check or resubmission requests
actions: Monitor the MCAS system's notifications screen for any state-level query after submission.
Investigate the flagged interrogatory against source data and correct the workbook if valid.
Resubmit the corrected line and capture the new confirmation number.
Log the query, resolution and resubmission date on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: every post-submission query is resolved and, where correction was needed, a resubmission confirmation is on file.

checklist.step: Log exceptions where a deadline was missed or data was materially wrong
actions: Open a tracker issue for any late submission or material data correction, naming the state, line and root cause.
Assign an owner and a remediation date to prevent recurrence.
Escalate any submission still outstanding at the due date to the Head of Compliance the same business day.
checklist.done: every missed deadline or material error has a logged issue with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain remediation sign-off on any exception
actions: Review each logged exception's root cause and remediation plan.
Confirm the remediation date is realistic against next year's filing calendar milestones.
Sign and date the tracker issue as closed once remediation evidence is attached.
checklist.done: every exception carries a dated Head of Compliance sign-off before being marked closed.

checklist.step: Retain the MCAS filing package per the retention schedule
actions: Move the workbook, confirmation PDF, certification and reconciliation note into the compliance evidence repository under company/line/year.
Apply the retention label matching the state market conduct exam look-back period (minimum 5 years, extended for an open exam).
Confirm the repository index is searchable by company code, state and reporting year.
checklist.done: the full MCAS package is filed, labelled for retention and retrievable by company code and year.

checklist.step: Brief Market Conduct Compliance on notable results
actions: Summarize year-over-year MCAS metric movements (complaint ratios, claim closure times, non-renewal rates) by state.
Flag any state/line where the company's metrics diverge materially from the prior year's national NAIC benchmark.
Present the summary at the next conduct-metrics monitoring cycle meeting.
checklist.done: a summary of MCAS results and flagged divergences is presented and minuted.

checklist.step: Update the MCAS procedure for next year's data call changes
actions: Compare this year's MCAS Definitions & Instructions to the prior year and note any new/retired interrogatories or line additions.
Update the internal MCAS filing procedure and the data extract mapping to reflect the changes.
Route the updated procedure to the Head of Compliance for annual approval.
checklist.done: the filing procedure and extract mapping are updated for next year's data call and approved.

testing.step: Build the population of MCAS submissions due for the year
actions: Pull the full list of company codes, states and lines of business required to file under the current MCAS data call.
Reconcile the list to the company's state licenses and lines actually written to confirm nothing in scope was omitted.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to licenses/lines written and signed as complete.

testing.step: Confirm every population row was actually submitted and on time
actions: Pull the submission status and timestamp for every company/state/line in the population from the MCAS system.
Compare each timestamp to the published due date and flag any late or missing submission as an exception.
testing.done: every population row has a confirmed on-time submission or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-trace a sample of submitted figures to source data
actions: Select a sample covering at least 3 states per line, weighted toward the largest premium states.
Independently re-pull premium, claims and complaint figures from the data warehouse for each sampled state/line.
Compare the re-pulled figures to the submitted MCAS workbook figures and note any mismatch.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and every sampled figure is compared to independently re-pulled source data.

testing.step: Recompute the reconciliation to the statutory Annual Statement
actions: For each sampled state/line, recompute the reconciliation between the MCAS submission and the corresponding Annual Statement schedule.
Confirm any variance is within the explained tolerance from the checklist reconciliation note.
testing.done: recomputed reconciliations match the filed explanation or are logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the internal review evidence exists for each sampled workbook
actions: Confirm a dated Regulatory Reporting Manager review log entry exists for each sampled company/line prior to submission.
Confirm large year-over-year variances (>25%) carry a written explanation.
testing.done: review evidence and variance explanations are present for every sampled workbook.

testing.step: Confirm deadline tracking and reminders were configured as designed
actions: Inspect the filing calendar for the tested year and confirm the T-30/T-15/T-7/T-2 milestones and escalation trigger exist for each line.
Confirm milestone completion dates in the tracker are consistent with the actual submission timestamps pulled earlier.
testing.done: reminder configuration and milestone completion are confirmed consistent with actual filing activity.

testing.step: Test the exception log for completeness
actions: Compare the late/incorrect submissions identified earlier to the exception tracker.
Confirm every identified issue has a corresponding tracker entry with root cause, owner and remediation date.
testing.done: no late or materially wrong submission is missing from the exception tracker.

testing.step: Confirm retention and retrievability of the filing package
actions: For each sampled company/line, retrieve the retained workbook, confirmation PDF, certification and reconciliation note.
Confirm the retention label meets the minimum 5-year (or exam-extended) requirement.
testing.done: the full package is retrievable and correctly labelled for every sampled item.

testing.step: Log and root-cause any testing exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every testing exception with its root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and add a mandatory retest for the next reporting year.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-late/zero-material-error threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the workpaper evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled submissions, sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly conduct-metrics monitoring cycle and its escalation into the board Conduct Review Committee established under ICA s.204.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Companies Act (Canada) s.204 (conduct review committee mandate), re-read each quarter against current OSFI market conduct expectations (rep: Canada).

In-scope processes.value: Complaints handling, claims cycle-time, non-renewal/cancellation and producer-conduct metrics across every province and US state the group writes business in.

In-scope systems.value: Conduct-metrics dashboard sourced from the Claims Platform, CRM and the complaint log.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metrics Monitoring Procedure — metric definitions, benchmark sources, escalation thresholds and committee reporting cadence.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board Conduct Review Committee; reviewed annually or on any OSFI/NAIC benchmark methodology change.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Dashboard finalized and pack circulated 10 business days before each quarterly Conduct Review Committee meeting.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar reminders at T-15 (data lock) and T-10 (pack circulation) before each committee meeting.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Dashboards, benchmark comparisons and committee minutes retained 7 years.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any metric breaching its threshold is logged with root cause and an assigned remediation owner.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off escalation calls and confirms adequacy of root-cause findings before committee circulation.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All four quarterly monitoring cycles in the audit year, across every province and US state in scope.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any flagged metric without a substantive, evidenced root cause is a fail; any pack circulated after T-10 without a logged exception is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; test samples one full quarter's cycle plus a walk-through of the other three.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared the dashboard or root-cause notes for the sampled quarter.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly conduct-metrics test workpaper filed in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Dashboard, exceptions tab, root-cause notes and committee minutes, presentable as an exam response within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns exam/inquiry responses; Chief Risk Officer clears any admission of an unresolved breach.

checklist.step: Define/refresh the metric set and regulatory benchmark sources
actions: Pull the current-year NAIC MCAS national median report and state regulator bulletins for complaint-ratio and claim-cycle-time benchmarks.
Confirm current OSFI market conduct expectations for the Canadian book.
Update the metric definitions spreadsheet with the refreshed benchmark sources.
Route the updated metric set to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for approval.
checklist.done: the metric set and benchmark sources are current and approved.

checklist.step: Extract quarterly conduct data
actions: Export claims cycle-time and closure data from the Claims Platform for the quarter by state/province and line.
Export complaint counts and categories from the complaint log.
Export policy counts from the Policy Administration Platform to compute per-1,000-policy ratios.
Reconcile record counts to the prior quarter's closing balance.
checklist.done: quarterly extracts are pulled and reconciled to policy counts.

checklist.step: Compute the metric ratios
actions: Load the extracts into the conduct-metrics dashboard template.
Compute complaints per 1,000 policies, average claim cycle time, non-renewal rate and producer-complaint rate by state/province.
Validate that totals foot to the source extracts.
Publish the draft dashboard.
checklist.done: all ratios compute correctly and foot to source extracts.

checklist.step: Compare each ratio to its benchmark
actions: Overlay the NAIC national median and OSFI expectation on each dashboard metric.
Flag any state/province/metric exceeding the benchmark by the defined tolerance (e.g., >150% of national median).
List flagged items on an exceptions tab.
checklist.done: every metric is compared to its benchmark with breaches flagged on the exceptions tab.

checklist.step: Root-cause each flagged metric
actions: Pull the underlying complaint or claim files for the flagged state/metric.
Interview the relevant claims or underwriting lead.
Document the root cause (staffing gap, system delay, product design issue).
Attach findings to the exceptions tab.
checklist.done: every flagged metric has a documented root cause.

checklist.step: Draft the quarterly conduct-metrics pack
actions: Compile the dashboard, exceptions tab and root-cause notes into the committee reporting pack.
Write an executive summary highlighting trend direction and open items from the prior quarter.
Route the pack to the Chief Risk Officer for review.
checklist.done: the pack is compiled with an executive summary and routed for review.

checklist.step: Chief Risk Officer review and escalation call
actions: Review the pack for any metric requiring escalation outside the quarterly cycle.
Confirm root causes are adequately supported.
Approve the pack for committee circulation or return it with required changes.
checklist.done: the CRO has approved the pack or returned it with documented changes.

checklist.step: Circulate the pack to the Conduct Review Committee
actions: Upload the approved pack to the board portal at least 10 business days before the meeting.
Confirm all committee members (none of whom may be officers or employees, per ICA s.204) have access.
Log the circulation date.
checklist.done: the pack is on the board portal at least 10 business days pre-meeting with circulation logged.

checklist.step: Present and minute the committee discussion
actions: Attend the Conduct Review Committee meeting and record the discussion of each flagged metric.
Capture any committee-directed remediation actions and owners.
Finalize the minutes within 5 business days of the meeting.
checklist.done: minutes capturing every flagged-metric discussion and directed action are finalized within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Assign and track remediation owners
actions: Open a tracker issue for each committee-directed remediation action, naming the owner and target date.
Link the issue to the exceptions tab row.
Set a review checkpoint for the next quarterly cycle.
checklist.done: every committee-directed action has a linked tracker issue with owner and target date.

checklist.step: Follow up on prior-quarter remediation status
actions: Pull the status of all open remediation issues from the prior quarter.
Confirm closed items have supporting evidence attached.
Carry forward any still-open item into the current pack's executive summary.
checklist.done: prior-quarter remediation status is confirmed and carried forward where still open.

checklist.step: Distribute the dashboard to regional compliance leads
actions: Send the finalized dashboard and minutes extract to each regional/state compliance lead.
Request written acknowledgement of any metric affecting their region.
Log acknowledgements received.
checklist.done: regional leads have received the dashboard and acknowledgements are logged.

checklist.step: Update escalation thresholds annually
actions: Review the year's benchmark breach frequency against current thresholds.
Adjust thresholds that proved too loose or too noisy.
Document the rationale and route to the Conduct Review Committee for approval.
checklist.done: thresholds are reviewed annually with a documented, committee-approved rationale for any change.

checklist.step: Log any missed reporting cycle as an exception
actions: If the pack is not circulated by T-10, open an exception with root cause and a corrective action.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: any missed T-10 circulation is logged as an exception with root cause and correction.

checklist.step: Retain the quarterly evidence package
actions: File the dashboard, exceptions tab, pack, minutes and tracker issues in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm searchability by quarter and state.
checklist.done: the full quarterly package is retained, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly monitoring cycles for the year
actions: List all four quarterly cycles due in the audit year.
Confirm a dashboard, pack and minutes exist for each.
testing.done: the population of four cycles is confirmed complete or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Reconcile dashboard figures to independently re-pulled source data
actions: For one sampled quarter, independently re-extract claims cycle-time, complaint and policy-count data for two sampled states.
Recompute the ratios and compare to the published dashboard.
testing.done: independently recomputed ratios match the published dashboard or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Re-test the benchmark comparison logic
actions: Independently source the NAIC national median and OSFI benchmark used for the sampled quarter.
Confirm the dashboard used the correct, current benchmark value.
testing.done: benchmark values used are confirmed current and correctly sourced.

testing.step: Verify root-cause documentation for sampled exceptions
actions: Pull the root-cause notes for every flagged metric in the sampled quarter.
Confirm each is substantive and supported by underlying claim/complaint files.
testing.done: every sampled root cause is substantive and evidenced.

testing.step: Confirm committee circulation timing
actions: Check the board portal's upload timestamp against the meeting date for the sampled quarter.
Confirm the 10-business-day requirement was met.
testing.done: circulation timing meets the 10-business-day requirement or is logged as a missed-deadline exception.

testing.step: Trace committee-directed actions to tracker issues
actions: Read the sampled quarter's minutes for every directed remediation action.
Confirm a matching tracker issue exists with the correct owner and target date.
testing.done: every minuted action traces to a tracker issue with matching owner and date.

testing.step: Verify remediation follow-through
actions: For tracker issues due before the audit date, confirm they are closed with evidence, or still open with a current, non-overdue target date.
testing.done: no remediation issue is overdue without an escalation on file.

testing.step: Confirm regional lead acknowledgement
actions: Sample two regional compliance leads and confirm their acknowledgement of the sampled quarter's dashboard is logged.
testing.done: acknowledgement evidence exists for the sampled regional leads.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every testing exception with root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and a retest commitment for next quarter's cycle.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, root cause, owner and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report to the Conduct Review Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and was reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Build/maintain the exam-readiness file inventory
actions: List every file category an examiner would request: procedures, complaint logs, claim samples, related-party approvals under ss.522-528, producer licensing records, advertising files.
Assign a named owner per category in the GRC platform.
Confirm coverage across every state/province the group writes in.
checklist.done: the inventory in the GRC platform names an owner for every exam file category and jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Capture related-party transaction approvals as they occur
actions: Pull the Conduct Review Committee's determination record for each related-party transaction approved under ss.522-528.
Confirm the record states the terms were at least as favourable as a market transaction.
File the determination in the exam-readiness folder within 5 business days.
checklist.done: every ss.522-528 determination is filed within 5 business days of approval.

checklist.step: Refresh the current procedures library
actions: Pull the latest approved version of every market-conduct procedure (complaints handling, claims practices, underwriting practices).
Confirm version and approval date match the document control log.
Replace superseded versions in the exam folder.
checklist.done: the exam folder holds only the current, approved version of every procedure.

checklist.step: Maintain the rolling complaint file sample
actions: Pull a rolling 12-month extract of closed complaints from the complaint log each month.
Select a representative cross-section by state and category.
Assemble the complaint file (intake, correspondence, resolution) for each selected item.
checklist.done: a current rolling 12-month complaint sample is assembled and refreshed monthly.

checklist.step: Maintain the rolling claims practice file sample
actions: Pull a monthly rolling sample of closed claims from the Claims Platform, stratified by state and line.
Assemble the claim file (intake, investigation notes, payment/denial letter) for each sampled claim.
checklist.done: a current rolling claims sample is assembled and refreshed monthly.

checklist.step: Maintain producer licensing and appointment records
actions: Pull the current appointment and license status for every active producer from NIPR.
Reconcile to the agency/producer management system.
File any discrepancy as an open item until resolved.
checklist.done: producer licensing records are current and reconciled monthly.

checklist.step: Maintain advertising and marketing material approvals
actions: Confirm every piece of consumer-facing advertising in current use has a documented compliance approval on file.
Pull any new material issued since the last check and file its approval.
checklist.done: every in-use advertising item has a filed compliance approval.

checklist.step: Run the monthly file-currency check
actions: Run the file-currency report showing each category's last-updated date.
Flag any category not updated within its required cadence.
Notify the named owner.
checklist.done: the monthly currency report is run and every flagged category has a notified owner.

checklist.step: Remediate flagged stale files
actions: Refresh the flagged file within 10 business days of notification.
Update the last-updated date in the GRC platform.
Note the reason for the delay if outside the 10-day window.
checklist.done: flagged files are refreshed within 10 business days or the delay is documented.

checklist.step: Conduct a quarterly self-mock-exam walkthrough
actions: Role-play a market conduct examiner's typical document request list against the current file inventory.
Time how long it would take to produce each item.
Log any item that could not be produced within 5 business days.
checklist.done: a quarterly mock-exam walkthrough is completed with a logged production-time result per item.

checklist.step: Escalate persistent gaps to Regulatory Attorney
actions: For any item that failed the mock-exam walkthrough twice in a row, escalate to the Regulatory Attorney with the gap description and proposed fix.
checklist.done: repeat gaps are escalated with a proposed fix.

checklist.step: Maintain the related-party transaction register cross-reference
actions: Cross-check the exam folder's ss.522-528 determinations against the Conduct Review Committee's official register.
Resolve any determination present in one but not the other.
checklist.done: the exam folder and committee register agree on every related-party determination.

checklist.step: Log exceptions for missing or stale files
actions: Open a tracker issue for any file that remains stale or missing past its remediation window.
Assign root cause and owner.
checklist.done: every persistent gap has a tracker issue with root cause and owner.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Attorney sign-off on the annual readiness attestation
actions: Review the year's mock-exam results and open exceptions.
Sign an annual attestation that the exam-readiness file set meets the standard, noting any residual gap and its plan.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation exists, noting residual gaps and plans.

checklist.step: Retain and index the exam-readiness archive
actions: Archive superseded file versions with their retirement date.
Apply the state look-back retention label (minimum 5 years, extended for open exams).
Confirm the archive is searchable by category, state and date.
checklist.done: the archive is retained, labelled and searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of exam-file categories and jurisdictions
actions: Pull the full category/jurisdiction inventory from the GRC platform.
testing.done: the population of categories/jurisdictions is confirmed against the compliance procedure's required list.

testing.step: Sample categories across jurisdictions
actions: Select a sample covering every file category in at least 3 states/provinces including the largest premium jurisdiction.
testing.done: the sample spans every category and at least 3 jurisdictions.

testing.step: Independently run the mock-exam request against the sample
actions: Request each sampled file cold, without prior notice to the file owner, and time the production.
testing.done: production time for each sampled item is independently timed and compared to the 5-business-day standard.

testing.step: Verify related-party determinations trace to the committee register
actions: For each sampled ss.522-528 determination, confirm it appears in the Conduct Review Committee's official register with matching terms and approval date.
testing.done: every sampled determination matches the committee register.

testing.step: Re-verify procedure currency
actions: Compare the version/date of each sampled procedure to the document control log's current approved version.
testing.done: every sampled procedure matches the current approved version or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-verify complaint and claims sample currency
actions: Confirm the sampled complaint and claims files reflect a rolling 12-month/monthly window.
Independently re-pull two items to confirm accuracy.
testing.done: sample currency and accuracy are confirmed for the tested items.

testing.step: Verify producer licensing reconciliation
actions: Independently pull two producers' NIPR status and compare to the file.
testing.done: sampled producer records match NIPR status.

testing.step: Test the currency-check and remediation process
actions: Confirm the monthly currency report ran for every tested month and flagged items were remediated within 10 business days per the log.
testing.done: currency checks ran on schedule and remediation timing meets the standard.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for each production-time failure or mismatch, with root cause, owner and remediation date.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue with root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 5-business-day production standard.
Write the conclusion.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report to the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Intake the finding and open a remediation record
actions: Log the finding source (OSFI supervisory letter, NAIC exam report, internal audit report, or appointed actuary s.369 report), the exact finding text and the citing provision.
Open a tracker record with a unique remediation ID.
checklist.done: a tracker record exists with the finding text, source and citing provision.

checklist.step: Classify severity and assign the accountable owner
actions: Rate the finding's severity against the internal severity matrix (regulatory breach, control weakness, documentation gap).
Assign the accountable business owner responsible for the underlying process.
checklist.done: severity is rated and an accountable owner is assigned.

checklist.step: Negotiate and record the agreed remediation date
actions: Where the finding came from OSFI or a state regulator, confirm the agreed remediation date in the regulator's letter or exam report.
Where it came from the appointed actuary under s.369, confirm the date agreed with the CEO/CFO.
Enter the exact date into the tracker.
checklist.done: the agreed remediation date is entered exactly as communicated by the source.

checklist.step: Build the remediation plan
actions: Have the accountable business owner document root cause, corrective actions, interim mitigations and a target completion date at or before the agreed regulator date.
Review the plan for adequacy against the finding.
checklist.done: a remediation plan with root cause, actions and target date is documented and reviewed.

checklist.step: Escalate any finding where root cause implicates financial condition
actions: Where the finding relates to a matter with material adverse effect on financial condition per s.369, notify the CFO and CEO in writing per the appointed actuary's escalation path.
Confirm receipt.
checklist.done: any s.369-triggering finding is escalated to CEO/CFO with confirmed receipt.

checklist.step: Track interim mitigations until the fix lands
actions: Implement and document any interim control (manual review, added sign-off) named in the remediation plan.
Update the tracker with mitigation status monthly until the permanent fix closes the finding.
checklist.done: interim mitigations are documented and status-updated monthly.

checklist.step: Set and monitor tracker milestones
actions: Enter T-30/T-10/T-2 reminder milestones ahead of the agreed remediation date.
Monitor milestone completion and chase the accountable owner if a milestone slips.
checklist.done: milestones are set and monitored, with chasing evidence for any slip.

checklist.step: Test the fix before declaring closure
actions: Request evidence that the corrective action operated as designed (e.g., a sample of transactions processed under the new control).
Confirm the evidence covers a period after the fix went live.
checklist.done: post-fix evidence confirms the corrective action is operating.

checklist.step: Route closure evidence to the Compliance Manager for review
actions: Collect the remediation plan, implementation evidence and post-fix test evidence.
Resolve any follow-up questions before closure is considered.
checklist.done: complete closure evidence is submitted and follow-up questions are answered.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Audit Executive sign-off on closure
actions: Review the closure package against the original finding and the agreed date.
Confirm the fix addresses the root cause, not just the symptom.
Sign and date the closure.
checklist.done: the Chief Audit Executive has signed and dated the closure, confirming root-cause coverage.

checklist.step: Report closure back to the finding's source
actions: Send the closure confirmation to OSFI, the state regulator, internal audit or the appointed actuary as applicable, referencing the original finding.
Retain the transmittal.
checklist.done: closure is formally reported back to the finding's source with a retained transmittal.

checklist.step: Escalate any finding at risk of missing its date
actions: Where a T-10 milestone shows the fix will not land on time, escalate to the Head of Compliance.
For regulator-sourced findings, prepare an extension request with justification.
checklist.done: at-risk findings are escalated before the agreed date with an extension request where needed.

checklist.step: Log a missed-deadline exception where remediation runs late
actions: Where a finding is not closed by its agreed date without an approved extension, log it as a compliance exception with root cause.
Notify the Chief Audit Executive.
checklist.done: any missed date without an approved extension is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Maintain the open-findings register for governance reporting
actions: Maintain a live register of open findings, ages and days-to-due.
Present the register to the Audit Committee/Conduct Review Committee at each scheduled meeting.
checklist.done: the open-findings register is current and presented at each governance meeting.

checklist.step: Retain the full remediation file
actions: File the finding, plan, evidence, closure sign-off and regulator transmittal under the remediation ID.
Apply 7-year retention.
checklist.done: the full remediation file is retained under its ID with 7-year labelling.

testing.step: Build the population of findings opened and due in the period
actions: Extract every tracker record opened or with an agreed date in the audit period, across all sources (OSFI, NAIC, internal audit, appointed actuary).
testing.done: the population is extracted and reconciled to the source exam/report list.

testing.step: Confirm every finding has a recorded agreed date matching its source document
actions: Compare the tracker's agreed date to the original regulator letter or exam report for each population item.
testing.done: every agreed date matches its source document or is logged as a discrepancy.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of findings still open past their agreed date, plus a random sample of 15 closed findings.
testing.done: the sample includes all overdue findings and 15 randomly selected closed findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the root-cause and fix adequacy assessment
actions: Independently assess whether the documented corrective action addresses the root cause rather than a symptom, for each sampled finding.
testing.done: an independent adequacy assessment is recorded for every sampled finding.

testing.step: Trace closure evidence for sampled closed findings
actions: Verify the post-fix test evidence exists and covers a period after implementation, for each sampled closed finding.
testing.done: post-fix evidence is verified for every sampled closed finding.

testing.step: Verify Chief Audit Executive sign-off exists and pre-dates the reported closure date
actions: Confirm a dated sign-off exists in the tracker for each sampled closed finding, before the closure was reported to the source.
testing.done: sign-off exists and pre-dates reported closure for every sampled item.

testing.step: Verify escalation occurred for s.369-triggering findings
actions: For sampled findings tagged as material adverse effect on financial condition, confirm CEO/CFO notification evidence exists.
testing.done: escalation evidence exists for every sampled s.369-triggering finding.

testing.step: Test overdue findings for exception logging and escalation
actions: Confirm every finding open past its agreed date has a logged exception, root cause and Chief Audit Executive notification.
testing.done: every overdue finding has a logged exception and notification.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for each testing exception with root cause, owner and remediation date.
Add a retest commitment.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, root cause, owner and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate against the zero-unapproved-late threshold.
Write the conclusion.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report results to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Confirm the applicable capital formula per legal entity
actions: List every legal entity and its home regulator (OSFI, state DOI via NAIC, BMA, national regulator under Solvency II).
Confirm the current formula version in force (current-year OSFI LICAT/MCT guideline, NAIC RBC formula edition, BSCR model, SCR standard formula/internal model).
checklist.done: every entity's applicable formula and current version is confirmed and logged.

checklist.step: Assemble the input data set
actions: Pull in-force policy data, reserves, asset holdings and reinsurance recoverables from the actuarial data mart for the valuation date.
Reconcile asset totals to the general ledger/custodian statements.
Reconcile reserve totals to the actuarial valuation system.
checklist.done: the input data set is reconciled to GL/custodian and the valuation system.

checklist.step: Run the capital model for each entity
actions: Load the reconciled inputs into the LICAT/MCT, RBC, BSCR or SCR module as applicable.
Execute the run and capture the model version and run log.
checklist.done: a capital run with logged model version exists for every entity.

checklist.step: Validate model outputs against prior-period trend
actions: Compare the current ratio (LICAT, MCT, RBC, BSCR, SCR coverage) to the prior quarter.
Investigate any movement exceeding the defined tolerance (e.g., ±10 percentage points) before accepting the run.
checklist.done: any out-of-tolerance movement is investigated and explained before acceptance.

checklist.step: Reconcile available capital to statutory capital resources
actions: Reconcile the model's available capital figure to statutory surplus/equity per the entity's statutory financial statements.
Adjust for regulator-specific tiering rules (Tier 1/Tier 2 capital) and document the adjustments.
checklist.done: available capital reconciles to statutory financial statements with tiering adjustments documented.

checklist.step: Independently review the calculation
actions: Re-perform key judgement points (asset risk factor selection, mortality/lapse assumption application, diversification credit) on a sample basis.
Confirm the model configuration matches the approved procedure.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary's independent review is documented with no unresolved discrepancy.

checklist.step: Aggregate to group capital adequacy
actions: Apply the group capital aggregation methodology combining each entity's surplus capital and required capital.
Adjust for intra-group transactions and diversification per the group's approved methodology.
checklist.done: the group capital position is aggregated per the approved methodology.

checklist.step: Populate the regulator-specific return template
actions: For the NAIC RBC entity, populate the RBC formula pages (Schedule XR / RBC filing software) with the model outputs.
For the OSFI entity, populate the LICAT/MCT return in OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System format.
For BMA and EIOPA entities, populate the respective statutory return templates.
checklist.done: every entity's regulator-specific return is populated from the reviewed model output.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO sign-off on the quarterly capital position
actions: Review the group and entity-level capital ratios against internal target and regulatory minimum.
Sign the quarterly capital position memo before it is used for any external communication.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed the quarterly capital position memo.

checklist.step: Route the annual calculation for board Audit/Risk Committee approval
actions: Present the full-year capital calculation, methodology and any assumption changes to the Audit or Risk Committee.
Obtain committee approval before filing.
checklist.done: the annual calculation has documented committee approval before filing.

checklist.step: Track each entity's statutory filing deadline
actions: Enter the specific statutory deadline for each entity's capital return into the filing calendar, computed from its financial year-end.
checklist.done: every entity's specific statutory deadline is in the filing calendar.

checklist.step: Configure deadline reminders
actions: Set T-10 and T-5 reminders against every entity's filing deadline, addressed to the Capital Model Actuary and Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
checklist.done: reminders are configured for every entity's deadline.

checklist.step: Log any calculation restatement or late filing as an exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for any post-filing restatement or missed deadline, naming root cause.
Assign an owner and remediation date.
checklist.done: every restatement or missed deadline is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary sign-off on remediation of any exception
actions: Review the exception's root cause and remediation plan.
Sign off before the issue is closed.
checklist.done: every exception carries a dated Chief Actuary sign-off before closure.

checklist.step: Retain the calculation package
actions: File the model run logs, input reconciliations, review notes, sign-offs and filed returns per entity per period.
Apply 7-year retention.
Confirm searchability by entity and period.
checklist.done: the full package is retained, labelled and retrievable by entity and period.

testing.step: Build the population of entity/period capital calculations due
actions: List every legal entity's quarterly and annual capital calculations required in the audit period.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the group's legal entity list and filing calendar.

testing.step: Reconcile input data independently for a sample
actions: For 3 sampled entity/periods, independently re-pull asset, reserve and reinsurance data.
Compare to the inputs used in the model run.
testing.done: independently re-pulled data matches the model inputs for every sampled entity/period, or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the capital calculation on the sample
actions: Using the same model version and inputs, re-run the calculation for the sampled entity/periods.
Compare the resulting ratio to the filed figure.
testing.done: re-performed ratios match the filed figures within rounding tolerance, or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform key judgement points independently
actions: For the sampled entity/periods, independently select and apply the asset risk factors, key assumptions and diversification credit.
Compare to the model's configuration.
testing.done: independent judgement matches the model configuration or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace available capital to statutory financial statements
actions: For each sampled entity/period, trace the available capital figure to the filed statutory financial statement.
Confirm tiering adjustments are correctly applied.
testing.done: available capital ties to the statutory statement with tiering correctly applied for every sampled item.

testing.step: Recompute the group aggregation
actions: Recompute the group capital roll-up from the sampled entity results using the approved aggregation methodology.
Compare to the reported group figure.
testing.done: recomputed group aggregation matches the reported figure or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify CFO and committee sign-offs exist and pre-date filing
actions: Confirm the CFO memo sign-off date and, for annual filings, the Audit/Risk Committee approval date both pre-date the actual regulator submission date.
testing.done: sign-off and approval dates pre-date submission for every sampled item.

testing.step: Confirm filing deadlines were met
actions: Compare each sampled entity's actual filing/submission date to its statutory deadline.
testing.done: every sampled filing met its deadline or a missed deadline is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every testing exception with root cause, owner and remediation date.
Add a retest commitment for the next cycle.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-deadline/zero-material-restatement threshold.
Write the conclusion.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report to the Audit/Risk Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit/Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Define the intervention ladder per entity
actions: Document each entity's regulator-defined intervention levels (OSFI Supervisory Target 100%/Minimum 90% LICAT or 150%/100% MCT, NAIC RBC Action Levels at 200%/150%/100%/70% of Authorized Control Level, BMA ECR trigger, Solvency II SCR 100%/MCR 100%).
Document the group's internal buffer above each (e.g., +25 percentage points).
checklist.done: the intervention ladder and internal buffer are documented for every entity.

checklist.step: Feed the monitoring dashboard from the latest capital calculation
actions: Pull the most recent quarterly (or interim, if triggered) capital ratio for every entity into the monitoring dashboard.
Timestamp the data source.
checklist.done: the dashboard reflects the latest calculated ratio per entity with a timestamp.

checklist.step: Run proxy monitoring between formal quarterly calculations
actions: Track material market movements (equity indices, interest rates, credit spreads) and large in-period transactions (dividends, capital injections, large claims).
Apply the approved proxy sensitivity to estimate the interim ratio when a material event occurs.
checklist.done: an interim proxy ratio is estimated and logged whenever a material market or transaction event occurs.

checklist.step: Compare each entity's ratio to its ladder and internal buffer
actions: Flag any entity within the internal buffer of a regulatory trigger as Amber.
Flag any entity below a regulatory trigger as Red.
checklist.done: every entity is Amber/Red flagged correctly against its own ladder.

checklist.step: Escalate an Amber flag internally
actions: Notify the CFO and the entity's Head of Capital Management the same business day an Amber flag is raised.
Open a watch-item in the monitoring log.
checklist.done: same-day CFO notification and a watch-item exist for every Amber flag.

checklist.step: Escalate a Red flag to the CEO and CFO immediately
actions: Notify the CEO the same business day.
Convene the CFO/Chief Risk Officer/Chief Actuary to assess cause and options (capital injection, reinsurance, business mix change, dividend suspension).
checklist.done: same-day CEO notification and a documented options assessment exist for every Red flag.

checklist.step: Notify the regulator per its required notice period
actions: For an OSFI-regulated entity, prepare the Superintendent notification per s.515 supervisory expectations.
For a US entity crossing an NAIC RBC Action Level, prepare the state DOI notification and corrective action plan filing required at that level.
Route through Regulatory Counsel before sending.
checklist.done: regulator notification is sent within the required notice period with Regulatory Counsel clearance.

checklist.step: Confirm the appointed actuary's parallel reporting duty is met
actions: Where the breach constitutes a material adverse effect on financial condition, prepare the actuary's own report to the CEO and CFO under s.369.
If unaddressed, report to the directors and Superintendent under s.368/s.369.
checklist.done: the appointed actuary's s.369 report is filed alongside the CFO's escalation where the threshold is met.

checklist.step: Build and approve the capital restoration plan
actions: Draft the plan restoring the ratio above the internal buffer, with actions, owners and a timeline.
Route to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer for approval.
Where regulator-mandated (e.g., NAIC RBC corrective action plan), align to that filing's required content.
checklist.done: a restoration plan with actions, owners and timeline is approved and, where mandated, filed with the regulator.

checklist.step: Track restoration progress weekly until cleared
actions: Update the monitoring log weekly with actual ratio movement against the restoration plan's projected path.
Report status to the CFO.
checklist.done: weekly progress updates exist until the ratio clears the internal buffer.

checklist.step: Confirm board notification for any Red flag
actions: Circulate the Red flag notice and restoration plan to the board within 5 business days.
Log board acknowledgement or discussion.
checklist.done: the board is notified within 5 business days with logged acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Close out the flag once restored
actions: Confirm two consecutive calculation cycles show the ratio above the internal buffer before downgrading the flag to Green.
Document the closure.
checklist.done: closure is documented only after two consecutive cycles clear the buffer.

checklist.step: Log every flag event in the monitoring log
actions: Record entity, date, ratio, trigger crossed, escalation actions and closure date for every flag event of the period.
checklist.done: a complete flag-event log exists for the period.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Risk Officer sign-off on the monitoring log quarterly
actions: Review the quarter's flag events and escalation evidence.
Sign off that escalation and notification requirements were met for every event.
checklist.done: quarterly sign-off confirms escalation/notification compliance for every flag event.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring and escalation record
actions: File the monitoring log, restoration plans, regulator notifications and board records.
Apply 7-year retention.
checklist.done: the monitoring and escalation record is retained and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of flag events in the period
actions: Extract every Amber/Red flag event logged in the monitoring log for the audit period.
testing.done: the flag-event population is extracted and reconciled to the quarterly capital calculations for the period.

testing.step: Independently recompute the intervention ladder comparison
actions: For each sampled entity/period, independently compare the filed ratio to the regulator's published trigger and the documented internal buffer.
testing.done: independent flag classification matches the logged classification or a difference is noted.

testing.step: Trace escalation timing for sampled Amber/Red events
actions: Compare the logged notification date/time to the flag date for CFO, CEO and board notifications.
Confirm same-business-day (internal) and required-notice-period (regulator) timing.
testing.done: escalation timing meets the required standard for every sampled event or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify regulator notification content and clearance
actions: Pull the actual regulator notification/filing for sampled Red events.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel clearance evidence exists and content matches the required corrective-action filing format.
testing.done: regulator notifications are cleared and correctly formatted for every sampled Red event.

testing.step: Verify the appointed actuary's parallel report where applicable
actions: Confirm a s.369 actuary report exists for every sampled event meeting the material-adverse-effect threshold.
testing.done: the actuary report exists for every applicable sampled event or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify restoration plan approval and tracking
actions: Confirm the restoration plan for each sampled Red event was approved by CFO and Chief Risk Officer.
Confirm weekly progress updates exist through closure.
testing.done: restoration plan approval and weekly tracking exist for every sampled event.

testing.step: Verify closure criteria were actually met
actions: Confirm two consecutive calculation cycles above the internal buffer exist before the logged closure date, for each sampled closed event.
testing.done: closure criteria are independently confirmed for every sampled closed event.

testing.step: Verify board notification for sampled Red events
actions: Confirm board portal upload and acknowledgement within 5 business days for each sampled Red event.
testing.done: board notification timing is confirmed for every sampled Red event.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every testing exception with root cause, owner and remediation date.
Add a retest commitment.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-late-escalation threshold.
Write the conclusion.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report to the Audit/Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Confirm the filing requirement and template version per entity
actions: For each legal entity, confirm the current-year statutory return template/instructions from its regulator (OSFI RRS filing specification, NAIC RBC filing software edition, BMA return, EIOPA QRT taxonomy version).
Note any year-over-year template change.
checklist.done: the current template/instructions are confirmed and any change is noted, per entity.

checklist.step: Pull the reviewed capital calculation output
actions: Take the CFO-signed capital position (from the capital calculation item) as the source figures.
Confirm the sign-off date and version match the filing period.
checklist.done: the source figures are the CFO-signed, version-matched output for the filing period.

checklist.step: Populate the regulator return
actions: Enter the figures into the OSFI RRS return, NAIC RBC filing software, BMA return or EIOPA QRT as applicable, field by field per the current instructions.
Run the template's built-in edit checks.
checklist.done: the return is populated and passes the template's edit checks.

checklist.step: Independently review the populated return
actions: Re-trace every field to the signed capital calculation source.
Confirm no manual override was made without a documented reason.
checklist.done: every field is traced to source and any override is documented.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO final sign-off before submission
actions: Review the completed return.
Sign the internal filing authorization form.
checklist.done: a signed CFO filing authorization exists before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the return through the regulator's system
actions: Log in to the regulator's filing system (OSFI RRS, NAIC filing portal, BMA portal, national EIOPA gateway) with the entity's credentials.
Upload/submit the return.
Capture the confirmation number and timestamp.
checklist.done: a submission confirmation number and timestamp are captured for every entity's return.

checklist.step: File the submission confirmation
actions: Save the confirmation receipt and the as-filed return copy to the filing folder.
Link to the CFO authorization.
checklist.done: the confirmation receipt and as-filed copy are saved and linked to the authorization.

checklist.step: Track each entity's statutory deadline
actions: Enter each entity's exact statutory due date into the filing calendar, computed from its financial year-end per the applicable statute.
checklist.done: every entity's exact due date is in the filing calendar.

checklist.step: Configure deadline reminders
actions: Set T-30/T-15/T-5 reminders per entity, addressed to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and CFO.
checklist.done: reminders are configured for every entity's due date.

checklist.step: Respond to regulator queries on the filed return
actions: Monitor the regulator's filing system for any query or request for correction.
Investigate against source data and prepare a response or amended filing within the regulator's stated window.
checklist.done: every query is answered or an amended filing is submitted within the regulator's stated window.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed return to the statutory financial statements
actions: Compare the filed capital return figures to the corresponding lines in the statutory Annual Statement or IFRS/local GAAP financial statements filed for the same period.
Document any timing or scope difference.
checklist.done: the filed return reconciles to the statutory financial statements with differences documented.

checklist.step: Log a late or amended filing as an exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for any filing submitted after its statutory deadline or requiring amendment, with root cause.
checklist.done: every late or amended filing is logged with root cause.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO sign-off on remediation of any exception
actions: Review the root cause and corrective action (e.g., earlier data lock, template change alert).
Sign off before closure.
checklist.done: every exception carries a dated CFO sign-off before closure.

checklist.step: Brief the Board on the filed capital position
actions: Summarize the filed ratios per entity and any exception for the next board or Audit Committee meeting.
checklist.done: a filed-capital-position summary is presented to the board.

checklist.step: Retain the filing package
actions: File the as-filed return, confirmation, CFO authorization and reconciliation per entity per year.
Apply 7-year retention.
Confirm searchability by entity and filing year.
checklist.done: the full filing package is retained, labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory filings due in the period
actions: List every entity's required capital/solvency filing and its statutory due date for the audit period.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the legal entity list and each regulator's filing requirement.

testing.step: Confirm every filing was submitted on time
actions: Pull the actual submission timestamp for each population item from the regulator's filing system.
Compare to the due date.
testing.done: every filing's timing is confirmed on-time or logged as a late-filing exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of late filings plus a random sample of 5 on-time filings across different regulators.
testing.done: the sample includes all late filings and 5 randomly selected on-time filings across regulators.

testing.step: Re-trace filed figures to the signed capital calculation
actions: For each sampled filing, trace every material field back to the CFO-signed capital calculation output.
testing.done: every sampled field traces to the signed source or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify the CFO filing authorization pre-dates submission
actions: Confirm the authorization sign-off date is before the submission timestamp for each sampled filing.
testing.done: authorization pre-dates submission for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Reconcile filed figures to the statutory financial statements
actions: Independently compare the sampled filing's figures to the corresponding statutory financial statement lines.
testing.done: figures reconcile or a documented difference exists for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Verify query responses were timely
actions: For any sampled filing with a regulator query, confirm the response or amended filing was submitted within the regulator's stated window.
testing.done: query responses meet the regulator's window for every sampled filing with a query.

testing.step: Verify exception logging for late filings
actions: Confirm every late filing identified earlier has a tracker issue with root cause and CFO sign-off.
testing.done: every late filing has a complete tracker issue with sign-off.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every testing exception with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.
testing.done: every testing exception has a complete issue record.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate against the zero-late threshold.
Write the conclusion.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Kick off the annual ORSA cycle and confirm scope
actions: Confirm the entities in scope (group and each OSFI-regulated entity).
Pull the current risk register from the GRC platform as the starting risk universe.
Confirm the planning horizon (typically 3-5 years) matches the business plan.
checklist.done: scope, risk universe and planning horizon are confirmed and documented.

checklist.step: Update the risk identification and assessment
actions: Refresh the risk register with any new or changed material risks (insurance, market, credit, operational, liquidity, strategic) since the prior ORSA.
Re-score likelihood and impact.
Confirm control owners have reviewed their entries.
checklist.done: the risk register is refreshed, re-scored and owner-confirmed for the current cycle.

checklist.step: Design the base and stress scenarios
actions: Define the base-case capital projection over the planning horizon using the approved business plan.
Define at least 3 stress scenarios (severe market downturn, mass lapse, catastrophic claims event) calibrated to the risk register's top risks.
Document scenario assumptions.
checklist.done: base and at least 3 documented stress scenarios exist, calibrated to the top risks.

checklist.step: Run the capital projections under each scenario
actions: Project the group and entity-level regulatory capital ratios (LICAT/MCT and other applicable formulas) under base and each stress scenario across the planning horizon.
Capture the model version and run log.
checklist.done: capital projections exist for base and every stress scenario, logged with model version.

checklist.step: Assess capital adequacy against risk appetite
actions: Compare the projected ratios in every scenario to the board-approved risk appetite thresholds and regulatory minimums.
Identify any scenario where the ratio would breach the internal buffer or a regulatory trigger.
checklist.done: every scenario is assessed against risk appetite and regulatory triggers, with breaches identified.

checklist.step: Identify management actions for adverse scenarios
actions: For every scenario showing a breach, document the management actions available (reinsurance, capital raise, business mix change, dividend suspension) and their expected effect on the ratio.
checklist.done: management actions and their expected effect are documented for every breaching scenario.

checklist.step: Draft the ORSA report
actions: Compile the risk assessment, scenario results, capital adequacy conclusion and management actions into the ORSA report using the current OSFI E-19 expected structure.
Route to the Chief Risk Officer for review.
checklist.done: a complete draft ORSA report is compiled and routed for CRO review.

checklist.step: Chief Risk Officer review
actions: Review the draft for completeness against E-19 expectations and internal consistency between the risk register and the scenarios modeled.
Return with required changes or approve for Risk Committee circulation.
checklist.done: the CRO has approved the draft or returned it with documented changes.

checklist.step: Circulate to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the draft ORSA to the board portal at least 6 weeks before the board approval meeting.
Schedule a Risk Committee review session.
checklist.done: the draft is on the board portal at least 6 weeks pre-meeting with a scheduled review session.

checklist.step: Incorporate Risk Committee feedback
actions: Log every Risk Committee comment.
Revise the report and scenario assumptions where directed.
Route the revised report back to the committee chair for confirmation before board submission.
checklist.done: all Risk Committee comments are logged, addressed and confirmed by the committee chair.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval
actions: Present the final ORSA to the board.
Record the board's approval (or conditions) in the minutes.
Capture the approval date.
checklist.done: board approval is recorded in the minutes with a captured approval date.

checklist.step: Prepare the OSFI-facing summary
actions: Prepare the ORSA summary/attestation in the form OSFI expects to receive on request under Guideline E-19.
Route through Regulatory Counsel before it is finalized.
checklist.done: an OSFI-ready summary is prepared and cleared by Regulatory Counsel.

checklist.step: Track the internal milestone calendar for the cycle
actions: Enter the T-60/T-30/T-10 milestones and the board approval date into the compliance filing calendar.
Monitor for slippage.
checklist.done: milestones are tracked in the calendar and monitored for slippage.

checklist.step: Log any missed milestone or OSFI request-response deadline
actions: Open a tracker issue for any missed internal milestone or a missed OSFI response deadline, with root cause and owner.
checklist.done: every missed milestone or deadline is logged with root cause and owner.

checklist.step: Retain the ORSA package
actions: File the risk register snapshot, scenario workpapers, draft/final ORSA, Risk Committee and board minutes, and the OSFI-ready summary.
Apply 7-year retention.
Confirm searchability by cycle year.
checklist.done: the full ORSA package is retained, labelled and retrievable by cycle year.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope entities for the ORSA cycle
actions: Confirm every OSFI-regulated entity required to be covered is included in the ORSA scope.
testing.done: the scope population is reconciled to the group's OSFI-regulated entity list.

testing.step: Independently re-check the risk register refresh
actions: Compare the current risk register to the prior cycle's.
Confirm at least the top 10 risks by score were reviewed and re-scored by their control owners.
testing.done: the top 10 risks show evidenced owner review and re-scoring.

testing.step: Re-perform one stress scenario calculation
actions: Independently reproduce the capital projection for one sampled stress scenario using the documented assumptions and model version.
Compare the result to the reported projection.
testing.done: the independently reproduced result matches the reported projection within tolerance, or a difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify scenario calibration against the risk register
actions: Confirm each of the documented stress scenarios maps to a top-scored risk in the register, not an arbitrary or stale scenario carried from a prior cycle.
testing.done: every stress scenario is confirmed to map to a current top risk.

testing.step: Verify management actions are credible and quantified
actions: For each breaching scenario, confirm the documented management action has a quantified expected effect on the ratio and a named owner.
testing.done: every breaching scenario's management action is quantified and owned.

testing.step: Verify board approval evidence
actions: Confirm the board minutes record explicit approval (or documented conditions).
Confirm the approval date is on or before the OSFI-facing summary's finalization date.
testing.done: board approval evidence is confirmed and correctly sequenced.

testing.step: Verify Risk Committee comment resolution
actions: Sample 5 logged Risk Committee comments.
Confirm each was addressed in the final report or explicitly declined with a documented reason.
testing.done: sampled comments are confirmed resolved or explicitly declined with reason.

testing.step: Verify the OSFI-facing summary was cleared by Regulatory Counsel
actions: Confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance exists for the finalized OSFI-ready summary.
testing.done: clearance evidence exists and pre-dates finalization.

testing.step: Log and root-cause testing exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every testing exception with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment for the next cycle.
testing.done: every testing exception has a complete issue record.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the workpaper evidence.
Have an independent reviewer sign and report results to the Board Risk Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Board Risk Committee.
